Commentary.Commentary: We're back! Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the openers. Sri Lanka Women are beginning with the spin of Malsha Shehani. A slip in place.
CHASE BEGINS...

121 in the first game, 128 in the second and 112 this evening. Sri Lanka’s scoring graph has steadily dipped as the series has progressed, barring a brief flicker of improvement last time out. India, on the other hand, have chased these targets without breaking a sweat. Will the script remain unchanged, or is there a twist waiting? Let’s find out.

Renuka Singh Thakur was the star of the show. Making her return to this format after a year, she looked a touch scratchy early on before turning up the heat and ripping through the line-up with a four-wicket haul. Deepti Sharma, back in the XI after missing the previous game due to illness, chipped in with three wickets of her own to draw level with Megan Schutt as the leading wicket-taker in Women’s T20Is. India Women were largely disciplined with their bowling plans, but there was a familiar blot on the copybook as three chances went down. A gentle reminder that they had spilled five in the opening game.

Sri Lanka Women went in with a cautious Powerplay plan, aiming to preserve wickets, but ended up losing three inside the first six overs. That early damage derailed their approach and they never quite found a way back. Imesha, Kavisha and Kaushini offered some resistance to drag the total past the 100-run mark, but overall it was another forgettable outing for the touring side.

Yet another dismal batting display from Sri Lanka Women. Compare the two halves and you do see a bit more intent after the 10-over mark, but the scoreboard once again tells a sorry story. Effort improved, numbers did not.
Drifting down the leg side, Kaushini Nuthyangana misses out as she tickles it straight to short fine. They cross for a run and Sri Lanka Women end on 112/7.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break. A cautious start from Sri Lanka, but it did not last for long. The wheels came off quickly as they lost the plot in the Powerplay, three wickets down and runs coming at a premium. Poor shot selection did not help the cause, and suddenly, they find themselves four down now. India have kept things tight and tidy, and after a slightly scratchy start on her return to T20Is, Renuka has bounced back in style with a three-wicket haul. Can the visitors regroup from here, or is this slide set to continue as the inning moves into the next phase? Kavisha Dilhari makes her way out to the centre.

This is bowled on a good length and pitches well outside off. Nilakshika Silva goes deep in the crease and moves a bit to the off side to flick but the ball darts back in sharply whilst keeping low. There's a huge appeal for LBW, which is turned down and the review is taken. No spike on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. The on-field umpire is asked to change her decision to OUT. Sri Lanka Women are 45 for 4 as Nilakshika Silva goes for a 9-ball 4.

Commentary.Commentary: Imesha Dulani walks in next with Sri Lanka Women in trouble after losing both the openers in quick succession.

OUT! CAUGHT! Renuka Singh Thakur strikes back and Hasini Perera has to walk back after a bright start. This is bowled a touch fuller from Renuka and the ball seams away from the left-hander. Perera plays away from the body and throws her hands at it but doesn't control the shot. The ball flies flat and straight to Deepti Sharma at short third, and she makes no mistake. Perera departs for 25 (18) and Sri Lanka Women are now 31/2.
Commentary.Howout: c Deepti Sharma b Renuka Singh Thakur
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, OUT! c Deepti Sharma b Renuka Singh Thakur.

Commentary.Commentary: No run there! On a good length, tighter in line around the off stump, Hasini looks to tap it in front of point and scamper for a single but Jemimah Rodrigues attacks the ball well and keeps it down to a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Edged away! Renuka bowls it back of a length and angles it wide of the off stump. Hasini Perera stays put and slashes hard, getting a thick outside edge that goes uppishly and well to the right of Vaishnavi Sharma at short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Renuka Singh Thakur returns to bowl the final over of the Powerplay. She went for 12 runs in her opening over.
Nice and full, on off stump, Samarawickrama drives it along the turf to mid off. A wicket and just 2 runs off that over from Deepti.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Deepti Sharma to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery around off, Harshitha Samarawickrama walks across to the off side and laps it through the fine leg region for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Deepti Sharma to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted delivery on the stumps, not all that full and this is eased back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Deepti Sharma to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Harshitha Samarawickrama walks in after the fall of the first wicket.

OUT! CAUGHT! Deepti Sharma gets the breakthrough and the Sri Lankan skipper has to walk back early. Sharma drags the length back by a few inches and bowls it around off stump. Chamari Athapaththu looks to reach for it and whack it back over the bowler's head but mistimes the lofted shot just over mid on. Harmanpreet Kaur takes a few steps back over there and pouches it safely. Athapaththu's sluggish knock comes to an end for 3 (12).
Commentary.Howout: c Harmanpreet Kaur b Deepti Sharma
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Deepti Sharma to Chamari Athapaththu, OUT! c Harmanpreet Kaur b Deepti Sharma.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery, pushed through outside off, Athapaththu cuts hard but hits it straight to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Deepti Sharma to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is tossed up, a bit fuller and outside off, Athapaththu eases it away in front of point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Deepti Sharma to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Deepti Sharma will continue from the opposite end. This already has been a better start from Sri Lanka Women.
FOUR! That's cheeky from Perera! On a good length and wide outside off, Hasini Perera shuffles well across the off stump and laps it skillfully over short fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Kranti Gaud to Hasini Perera, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: This is banged in shorter and just outside off, Hasini Perera rocks back and looks to pull but gets hurried and mistimes it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Kranti Gaud to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Did you know? Harmanpreet Kaur becomes the first captain to register 15 wins against a single opposition in Women’s T20Is, doing it all against Sri Lanka. A record built on consistency and calm leadership.
Good-length delivery on the pads, Athapaththu fails to flick it away and the ball rolls away after hitting the pads and goes behind square leg. They pick up a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: A tad fuller and around off, Chamari Athapaththu stays back in the crease and cuts hard but gets more of an outside edge down to short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and angled into the left-hander from well outside off, Athapaththu hangs back and tries to play the late cut but dabs it down to the right of the first slip fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kranti comes around the wicket and shortens the length, angling it into the batter. Chamari Athapaththu comes down the pitch and looks to make room and go through covers, but ends up jamming it into the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A touch short and around off, spinning way, Chamari plays with soft hands and dabs it in front of short third for a quick run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Deepti Sharma to Chamari Athapaththu, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This time Perera works it through square leg and rotates the strike. India have pulled things back well after a 12-run first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Deepti Sharma to Hasini Perera, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Again short and around off, Perera cuts but again fails to beat the fielder at point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Deepti Sharma to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and on middle, Hasini makes room and cuts but finds the backward point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Deepti Sharma to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: EDGY FOUR! Tossed up, full and teasing it outside off, Hasini Perera sinks low for the slog sweep but fails to time it well. It kisses the top edge and balloons over square leg. A couple of fielders give chase, plenty of effort, but the ball has the final say as it skips away to the rope.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Deepti Sharma to Hasini Perera, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Plenty of flight on this one as it dips towards a yorker length outside off, Hasini Perera drives it without much intent back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Deepti Sharma to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Will we see an early bowling change? Yes, we do. Deepti Sharma comes into the attack, replacing Renuka Singh Thakur.
Play and a miss, this time by Chamari Athapaththu. Kranti Gaud tempts the batter with a short ball outside off, Chamari tries to cut but fails to connect. Just 2 runs from this over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kranti goes short and into the batter, around off, Hasini goes back and pulls it through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Kranti Gaud to Hasini Perera, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flashes and misses! Width there, outside off, there to be hit but Hasini Perera fails to connect with her attempted cut shot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Kranti Gaud to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off, driven to covers. One more dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Kranti Gaud to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sliding down the leg side, the batter attempts to flick but gets a bit of inside edge. The ball rolls wide of the keeper and by the time Richa Ghosh picks it up to her right, they cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kranti Gaud begins with a full ball on off, Chamari drives off the front foot but finds mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Kranti Gaud to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kranti Gaud will share the new ball with Renuka Singh Thakur.

FOUR! Finds the gap and the fence. 12 from the first over. Again, Renuka is generous in providing room outside off and it's overpitched as well. Hasini Perera strides forward and drills it through covers. The sweeper in the deep rushes across to her left but fails to get to the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Misses out. Plenty of width outside off, Hasini throws her bat at it but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up and outside off, Chamari Athapaththu drives this time, in the gap at covers. There is a sweeper present, so only a run. The skipper opens her account.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Renuka Singh Thakur to Chamari Athapaththu, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The keeper comes up and Renuka bowls it on a shortish length around middle and off. Perera stays back and strokes it through covers for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Fine shot! This time, there is a bit of width outside off, Hasini Perera stays leg-side of this delivery and smashes it through point. It finds the gap and races away to find the fence as Kranti Gaud moves across to her right in the deep.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka Women are away with a couple of runs. Thakur begins with a delivery on the pads, full in length, Hasini flicks it a bit aerially but in the gap at mid-wicket. The ball travels to the deep and they take two runs. Better intent would have given them the third run as well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Renuka Singh Thakur to Hasini Perera, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and the Indian players can be seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Hasini Perera and Chamari Athapaththu to open the innings for Sri Lanka Women. Renuka Singh Thakur, who will be playing a T20I game after a whole year, will take the new ball for India. Let's play...

Sri Lanka Women have a debutant in their side for this game in the form of Nimasha Meepage and it will be interesting to see how the young left-arm spinner goes about her business. We are minutes away from the first ball, so stay tuned.

Smriti Mandhana, the star Indian player and vice-captain, gives a quick interview. Says it feels truly special to be called World Champions and admits that carrying that tag is an amazing feeling. She notes that it has been about a month now and feels the team has handled it really well. On crossing the 4000 run mark in T20Is in the last game, Smriti replies that it is good to reach the milestone but prefers not to dwell too much on her own batting. She explains that her focus remains firmly on this format. Further adds that although the team has been playing a lot of one-day cricket, they are well aware that the coming months will involve plenty of T20 cricket, with the World Cup and the WPL lined up.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Chamari Athapaththu (C), Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Imesha Dulani (in for Vishmi Gunarathne), Kaushini Nuthyangana (WK), Malsha Shehani (In for Kawya Kavindi), Inoka Ranaweera, Malki Madara, and Nimasha Meepage (In for Shashini Gimhani).

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma (In for Sneh Rana), Amanjot Kaur, Vaishnavi Sharma, Kranti Gaud, Renuka Singh Thakur (In for Arundhati Reddy), and Sree Charani.

Chamari Athapaththu, the Lankan captain, says they would have certainly chosen to bowl as well. Adds that she is confident in her bowling attack. Mentions that the message to the side is to play with freedom and feels this is a good opportunity for the young girls to step up and showcase their talent. She also informs that they have made THREE changes - Imesha Dulani, Malsha Shehani and Nimasha Meepage replace Vishmi Gunarathne, Kawya Kavindi and Shashini Gimhani.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the Indian skipper, smiles after winning her third toss on the trot and says the decision is to bowl first. She feels the dew will come into play later in the evening. Adds that the message to the team remains the same as the previous game, stressing that it is an important match and the aim is to finish on a high note. Also informs that the side goes in with a couple of changes - Deepti Sharma and Renuka Singh Thakur come in place of Sneh Rana and Arundhati Reddy.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and Chamari Athapaththu calls 'Heads.' It lands 'Tails,' and India will BOWL first.

As the sun sets over Kerala, all eyes will be on whether the visitors can stage a comeback or if India will march toward an emphatic series victory in front of a passionate home crowd. Please stay tuned for the toss and team news.

Sri Lanka, led by the veteran Chamari Athapaththu, finds itself in a must-win situation to keep the series alive. Despite showing flashes of brilliance, particularly from young Vishmi Gunarathne and the skipper herself, the Lankan batting lineup has struggled to convert starts into match-winning scores. The visitors will need a much more aggressive approach on a surface expected to be batting-friendly. Their bowling attack, spearheaded by the experienced Inoka Ranaweera, must also find a way to dismantle India’s formidable top three.

A win tonight would seal the five-match series with two games to spare, underscoring India's dominance at home. Their bowling unit has been particularly impressive, consistently restricting the visitors to sub-130 totals, while the top order has chased down targets with relative ease. India has already begun experimenting with their squad, handing a debut to a young talent like left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma. Deepti Sharma was out with a fever in the last game but expect her to be back as the home side looks to seal the deal.

Hello, and a warm welcome to one and all! The series shifts to the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram for the third T20I between India Women and Sri Lanka Women, with India firmly in the driver’s seat. Carrying the momentum of their recent ODI World Cup triumph, Harmanpreet Kaur’s side has been clinical, securing comfortable victories in the first two matches held in Visakhapatnam. The Lankans have it all to do and will be hoping for a turnaround in order to get back in this five-match series.
... MATCH DAY ...

From the eastern shoreline, we now head southwest coast of the country, to Kerala’s capital, the postcard-perfect city of Thiruvananthapuram, better known to most as Trivandrum. After a two-year-long wait, the Greenfield International Stadium is ready to come alive again, and this time it is for something truly special. For the first time ever, the venue will stage a women’s international match, a landmark moment that highlights how women’s cricket is steadily expanding its wingspan with every passing year. With a commanding 2-0 lead in the five-match series, India Women have been in complete control, outplaying their neighbors, Sri Lanka Women. It is do or die for the Lankan women, with another misstep all but sealing the series. The opening two games have delivered a harsh reality check, exposing just how heavily the side leans on their skipper Chamari Athapaththu. When she gets going, everything seems to fall into place. When she is subdued, the cracks show quickly. Batting first on both occasions and on surfaces tailor made for run scoring in Vizag, Sri Lanka could only muster 121 and 128, barely scraping past a run a ball. Numbers that tell a blunt story and ones that are a long way from being truly competitive. Their batting unit has been put through a severe trial by India’s spin attack, and the pressure has shown early. The opening pair of Athapaththu and Vishmi has managed just 20 runs across two matches, leaving the side constantly on the back foot. That has piled enormous pressure on the middle order, where Harshitha Samarawickrama has shown glimpses of promise but has not been able to kick on or shift gears. Hasini Perera has endured much the same fate, finding her feet but never quite finding the tempo. The fallout has been brutal for an inexperienced bowling group that has had far too less to defend and very little to show for its efforts, with defeats coming by heavy margins in both games. Kawya Kavindi, the seasoned Inoka Ranaweera and Malki Madara have all returned modest figures, but the blame can hardly rest on their shoulders. Without solid batting foundations, the bowlers have been fighting a battle that was lost long ago. The Women in Blue have shown real home dominance. Their bowling unit has clicked beautifully. Kranti Gaud and Arundhati Reddy have stepped up in keeping things tight inside the field restrictions, with the spinners leading the charge and keeping Sri Lanka on a tight leash in the middle phase. One of the standout stories has been the rise of Sree Charani, whose progress has been hard to miss. Vaishnavi Sharma too had a night to remember, opening her T20I account by luring out the dangerous Nilakshika Silva and finishing with a tidy two-wicket haul. No Deepti? No problem for India. A rare absence created an unexpected opening, and India barely felt the void. Even on the day Deepti was crowned the No. 1 T20I bowler in the ICC rankings, a mild fever ended her run of 92 consecutive appearances stretching back to 2019. The responsibility for control, usually entrusted to Deepti, was calmly assumed by Rana, who played her first T20I since 2016. Thrown straight into the deep end against a rampant Chamari Athapaththu, Rana rose to the challenge and delivered with assurance. Those bowling efforts have been well supported by the batters. Shafali Verma and Jemimah Rodrigues have carried the run scoring with a fifty apiece, while Smriti Mandhana will be keen to turn her promising starts into more substantial contributions in these three remaining games. The middle order has barely been tested as India won both games with a margin of 8 and 7 wickets respectively. But every day is not the same, and when the moment demands it, that engine room will need to step up as well. Across both departments, the contrast in quality and conviction between the two sides has been stark. While India have won both T20Is played this calendar year, it has been a forgettable run for Sri Lanka Women in the format, managing just one win from five outings. In terms of conditions, the Greenfield Stadium has hosted four men’s T20Is so far, with 235 being the highest first-innings total. Notably, this came in the most recent match at the venue, played between India and Australia, back in 2023. This indicates that the pitch is largely batter-friendly, especially when batting first, while still offering enough pace and bounce to keep stroke-makers interested throughout the innings. So, one can expect a high-scoring contest at this venue, particularly if the surface remains true, but bowling in the second innings can be a bit tricky with the dew settling in later on. Sri Lanka will be looking to maintain the pace with the bat, whereas India would like to settle their fielding lapses from the first two matches. A very crucial game of the series is on the cards. Expect tough competition from both sides.
